title: 03. Databases & Data Modeling: Database Indexing
summary: A database index is a data structure that improves the speed of data retrieval operations at the cost of additional writes and storage space.

sections.title: Detailed Explanation
sections.body:
### What is Database Indexing?

A **database index** is a data structure that improves the speed of data retrieval operations at the cost of additional writes and storage space. Think of it like a book index - instead of reading every page to find a topic, you look up the index to find the exact page.

### Why Indexing Matters

Without indexes:

```
SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = 'alice@example.com'
-- Full table scan: O(n) - check every row
-- 10 million rows = 10 million comparisons
```

With indexes:

```
-- B-Tree index lookup: O(log n)
-- 10 million rows = ~23 comparisons
```

### Types of Indexes

1. **Primary Index**: Created automatically on primary key
2. **Secondary Index**: Created on non-primary columns
3. **Unique Index**: Ensures uniqueness of values
4. **Composite Index**: Multiple columns combined
5. **Covering Index**: Contains all columns needed for a query
6. **Partial Index**: Index on subset of rows
7. **Full-Text Index**: For text search
8. **Spatial Index**: For geographic data

### Index Data Structures

**B-Tree (Most Common):**

- Balanced tree structure
- Good for equality and range queries
- Used by PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB

**Hash Index:**

- Fast equality lookups O(1)
- Cannot do range queries
- Used by Redis, some PostgreSQL cases

**LSM-Tree (Log-Structured Merge-Tree):**

- Optimized for write-heavy workloads
- Used by Cassandra, RocksDB, LevelDB

**GiST/GIN (Generalized Indexes):**

- Used for full-text, arrays, JSON
- PostgreSQL specialty

diagrams.title: Why an index turns a full scan into a few page reads
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  q["SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = 'a@x.com'"] --> c{"Index on email?"}
  c -->|no| scan["Full table scan: read all 10M rows"]
  c -->|yes| root["B-tree root page"]
  root --> inner["Internal page: a–m"]
  inner --> leaf["Leaf page: 'a@x.com' → row id 8812"]
  leaf --> row["Fetch 1 row from the heap"]
  scan --> slow["O(n): seconds"]
  row --> fast["O(log n): ~3–4 page reads, milliseconds"]
diagrams.explain: Without an index the database must read every row to find a match. A **B-tree index** keeps the column sorted in a shallow tree, so a lookup touches only a handful of pages even for millions of rows. The price: every insert and update must also update each index, and indexes take space — so index the columns you filter, join and sort on, not everything.

sections.title: Visual Explanation
sections.body:
### B-Tree Index Structure

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                            B-TREE INDEX STRUCTURE                                │
│                   (Used by PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB)                           │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Example: Index on "age" column

                                  ┌──────────────────┐
                             Root │   30  │   60     │
                                  └─────┬────┬───────┘
                                       │    │
                    ┌──────────────────┘    └──────────────────┐
                    │                                          │
                    ▼                                          ▼
          ┌─────────────────┐                      ┌─────────────────┐
 Internal │  10  │   20     │                      │  45  │   55     │
          └───┬─────┬────┬──┘                      └───┬─────┬────┬──┘
              │     │    │                             │     │    │
     ┌────────┘     │    └────────┐          ┌────────┘     │    └────────┐
     ▼              ▼             ▼          ▼              ▼             ▼
┌─────────┐   ┌─────────┐   ┌─────────┐ ┌─────────┐   ┌─────────┐   ┌─────────┐
│ 5,7,8   │──▶│ 12,15,18│──▶│ 21,25   │ │ 32,38,40│──▶│ 47,50,52│──▶│ 58,62   │
│ └─Leaf──│   │ └─Leaf──│   │ └─Leaf──│ │ └─Leaf──│   │ └─Leaf──│   │ └─Leaf──│
└────┬────┘   └────┬────┘   └────┬────┘ └────┬────┘   └────┬────┘   └────┬────┘
     │             │             │           │             │             │
     ▼             ▼             ▼           ▼             ▼             ▼
   Row IDs       Row IDs      Row IDs     Row IDs       Row IDs       Row IDs
  (pointers     (pointers    (pointers   (pointers     (pointers     (pointers
   to actual     to actual    to actual   to actual     to actual     to actual
   table rows)   table rows)  table rows) table rows)   table rows)   table rows)

Query: WHERE age = 25
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Step 1: Start at root → 25 < 30 → go left
Step 2: At internal node → 20 < 25 < 30 → go right
Step 3: At leaf → find 25 → get row pointer
Step 4: Fetch row from table

Time Complexity: O(log n) ≈ 3-4 comparisons for millions of rows
```

### How Indexes Speed Up Queries

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                          WITHOUT INDEX (Full Table Scan)                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Query: SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = 'bob@example.com'

Table (10 million rows):
┌────┬──────────────────────┬───────────────┐
│ ID │ Email                │ Name          │ ◀── Check each row
├────┼──────────────────────┼───────────────┤     until found
│  1 │ alice@example.com    │ Alice         │ ✗
│  2 │ bob@example.com      │ Bob           │ ✓ Found! (but continues)
│  3 │ carol@example.com    │ Carol         │ ✗
│ ...│ ...                  │ ...           │
│ 10M│ zack@example.com     │ Zack          │ ✗
└────┴──────────────────────┴───────────────┘

Time: O(n) = Check ALL 10 million rows
Disk I/O: Read entire table from disk

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                          WITH INDEX (B-Tree Lookup)                              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Index on email (sorted):
┌──────────────────────┬────────┐
│ Email (sorted)       │ Row ID │
├──────────────────────┼────────┤     B-Tree Navigation:
│ alice@example.com    │ 1      │     ┌───────────────┐
│ bob@example.com      │ 2 ◀────│────▶│ Root: m       │
│ carol@example.com    │ 3      │     └───────┬───────┘
│ ...                  │ ...    │             │ 'b' < 'm'
└──────────────────────┴────────┘             ▼
                                      ┌───────────────┐
                                      │ Internal: f   │
                                      └───────┬───────┘
                                              │ 'b' < 'f'
                                              ▼
                                      ┌───────────────┐
                                      │ Leaf: bob@... │──▶ Row ID: 2
                                      └───────────────┘

Time: O(log n) = ~23 comparisons for 10 million rows
Disk I/O: Read only index nodes + 1 row
```

### Composite Index Column Order

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    COMPOSITE INDEX: Column Order Matters!                        │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Index on (last_name, first_name, age)
                ↓
    Leftmost prefix matters!

Index Structure (sorted by: last_name → first_name → age):
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Adams, Alice, 30  → Adams, Bob, 25 → Brown, Alice, 40 → Brown, Bob, 35 → ...   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

✅ These queries CAN use the index:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

WHERE last_name = 'Adams'                     ✅ Uses first column
WHERE last_name = 'Adams' AND first_name = 'Alice'   ✅ Uses first two columns
WHERE last_name = 'Adams' AND first_name = 'Alice' AND age = 30  ✅ All columns
WHERE last_name = 'Adams' AND first_name > 'B'       ✅ Range on second column
WHERE last_name BETWEEN 'A' AND 'C'                  ✅ Range on first column

❌ These queries CANNOT use the index efficiently:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

WHERE first_name = 'Alice'                   ❌ Skips first column
WHERE age = 30                               ❌ Skips first two columns
WHERE last_name = 'Adams' AND age = 30       ⚠️ Only uses last_name (skips first_name)
WHERE first_name = 'Alice' AND age = 30      ❌ Neither is first column

💡 RULE: Index is used left-to-right, stops at first gap or range condition
```

### Covering Index

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                              COVERING INDEX                                      │
│            (Index contains ALL columns needed by query)                          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Query: SELECT email, name FROM users WHERE email = 'bob@example.com'

NON-COVERING INDEX (index on email only):
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1. Search Index          2. Table Lookup (extra I/O!)
┌──────────────────┐     ┌──────────────────────────────┐
│ email     │ ptr  │────▶│ id │ email      │ name  │... │
│ bob@...   │  2   │     │  2 │ bob@...    │ Bob   │    │
└──────────────────┘     └──────────────────────────────┘
       ↓                              ↓
  Index Scan              Random Disk Access (SLOW!)

COVERING INDEX (index on email, name):
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1. Search Index (all data here!)
┌────────────────────────────────┐
│ email          │ name   │ ptr │
│ bob@...        │ Bob    │  2  │
└────────────────────────────────┘
       ↓
  Index-Only Scan (no table access!)
  2-3x faster for covered queries

PostgreSQL: CREATE INDEX idx ON users(email) INCLUDE (name);
MySQL: CREATE INDEX idx ON users(email, name);
```

### Index Performance Trade-offs

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                         INDEX TRADE-OFFS                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

                    ┌─────────────┐
                    │ More Indexes│
                    └──────┬──────┘
                           │
         ┌─────────────────┼─────────────────┐
         ▼                 │                 ▼
    ┌─────────┐           │           ┌─────────────┐
    │ FASTER  │           │           │  SLOWER     │
    │ READS   │           │           │  WRITES     │
    └─────────┘           │           └─────────────┘
                          │
                ┌─────────┴─────────┐
                ▼                   ▼
         ┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐
         │ MORE        │     │ MORE        │
         │ STORAGE     │     │ MAINTENANCE │
         └─────────────┘     └─────────────┘

Write Overhead per Index:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

INSERT: Create entry in EACH index
UPDATE: Update entry in EACH affected index
DELETE: Remove entry from EACH index

Example: Table with 5 indexes
- 1 INSERT = 1 table write + 5 index writes = 6x work

When to Remove Indexes:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

• Unused indexes (check pg_stat_user_indexes)
• Duplicate/redundant indexes
• Indexes on frequently updated columns
• Low-cardinality columns (few unique values)
```

sections.title: Example 1: PostgreSQL Indexing Strategies
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- PostgreSQL Indexing Best Practices
- Complete guide to PostgreSQL indexing
- Create table for indexing demonstrations
- DROP TABLE IF EXISTS orders CASCADE; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS customers CASCADE;
- 1. Unique index (automatically created for PRIMARY KEY)
- 2. Non-unique B-tree index
- 3. Composite index (multi-column)
- 4. Partial index (only index subset of rows)

```python
"""
PostgreSQL Indexing Best Practices
"""

import psycopg2
from psycopg2.extras import RealDictCursor
from typing import List, Dict
import time

class PostgreSQLIndexing:
    """
    Complete guide to PostgreSQL indexing
    """

    def __init__(self, connection_string: str):
        self.conn = psycopg2.connect(connection_string)

    def create_sample_table(self):
        """Create table for indexing demonstrations"""
        with self.conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute("""
                DROP TABLE IF EXISTS orders CASCADE;
                DROP TABLE IF EXISTS customers CASCADE;

                CREATE TABLE customers (
                    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
                    email VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
                    name VARCHAR(255),
                    country VARCHAR(100),
                    segment VARCHAR(50),
                    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),
                    metadata JSONB
                );

                CREATE TABLE orders (
                    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
                    customer_id INTEGER REFERENCES customers(id),
                    order_date DATE NOT NULL,
                    total DECIMAL(10, 2),
                    status VARCHAR(50),
                    items JSONB
                );
            """)
            self.conn.commit()

    # ==================== BASIC INDEXES ====================

    def create_basic_indexes(self):
        """Different types of basic indexes"""
        with self.conn.cursor() as cur:
            # 1. Unique index (automatically created for PRIMARY KEY)
            cur.execute("""
                CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_customer_email
                ON customers(email);
            """)

            # 2. Non-unique B-tree index
            cur.execute("""
                CREATE INDEX idx_customer_country
                ON customers(country);
            """)

            # 3. Composite index (multi-column)
            cur.execute("""
                CREATE INDEX idx_orders_customer_date
                ON orders(customer_id, order_date DESC);
            """)

            # 4. Partial index (only index subset of rows)
            cur.execute("""
                CREATE INDEX idx_orders_pending
                ON orders(customer_id, order_date)
                WHERE status = 'pending';
            """)

            # 5. Index with INCLUDE (covering index)
            cur.execute("""
                CREATE INDEX idx_orders_status_include
                ON orders(status)
                INCLUDE (total, order_date);
            """)

            self.conn.commit()

    # ==================== EXPRESSION INDEXES ====================

    def create_expression_indexes(self):
        """Indexes on expressions/functions"""
        with self.conn.cursor() as cur:
            # Index on lower-case email for case-insensitive search
            cur.execute("""
                CREATE INDEX idx_customer_email_lower
                ON customers(LOWER(email));
            """)

            # Index on date extraction
            cur.execute("""
                CREATE INDEX idx_orders_year_month
                ON orders(EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date),
                         EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_date));
            """)

            # JSONB index on specific key
            cur.execute("""
                CREATE INDEX idx_customer_metadata_type
                ON customers((metadata->>'type'));
            """)

            self.conn.commit()

    # ==================== SPECIALIZED INDEXES ====================

    def create_specialized_indexes(self):
        """GIN, GiST, and BRIN indexes"""
        with self.conn.cursor() as cur:
            # GIN index for JSONB (contains, exists operators)
            cur.execute("""
                CREATE INDEX idx_customer_metadata_gin
                ON customers USING GIN(metadata);
            """)

            # GIN index for full-text search
            cur.execute("""
                ALTER TABLE customers ADD COLUMN search_vector tsvector;
                UPDATE customers SET search_vector =
                    to_tsvector('english', name || ' ' || COALESCE(country, ''));

                CREATE INDEX idx_customer_search
                ON customers USING GIN(search_vector);
            """)

            # GIN index for array contains
            cur.execute("""
                CREATE INDEX idx_orders_items_gin
                ON orders USING GIN(items);
            """)

            # BRIN index for naturally ordered data (timestamps)
            # Very compact, good for large tables with sorted data
            cur.execute("""
                CREATE INDEX idx_orders_date_brin
                ON orders USING BRIN(order_date);
            """)

            self.conn.commit()

    # ==================== CONCURRENT INDEXING ====================

    def create_index_online(self, table: str, columns: List[str], index_name: str):
        """
        Create index without blocking writes
        CRITICAL for production databases
        """
        # CONCURRENTLY doesn't work inside a transaction
        old_autocommit = self.conn.autocommit
        self.conn.autocommit = True

        try:
            with self.conn.cursor() as cur:
                col_str = ", ".join(columns)
                cur.execute(f"""
                    CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS {index_name}
                    ON {table}({col_str});
                """)
        finally:
            self.conn.autocommit = old_autocommit

    # ==================== INDEX ANALYSIS ====================

    def analyze_query(self, query: str) -> Dict:
        """Get query execution plan"""
        with self.conn.cursor(cursor_factory=RealDictCursor) as cur:
            cur.execute(f"EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, FORMAT JSON) {query}")
            plan = cur.fetchone()
            return plan

    def get_index_usage_stats(self) -> List[Dict]:
        """Find unused indexes"""
        with self.conn.cursor(cursor_factory=RealDictCursor) as cur:
            cur.execute("""
                SELECT
                    schemaname,
                    tablename,
                    indexname,
                    idx_tup_read,
                    idx_tup_fetch,
                    pg_size_pretty(pg_relation_size(indexrelid)) as index_size
                FROM pg_stat_user_indexes
                ORDER BY idx_tup_read DESC;
            """)
            return cur.fetchall()

    def find_missing_indexes(self) -> List[Dict]:
        """Suggest indexes based on sequential scans"""
        with self.conn.cursor(cursor_factory=RealDictCursor) as cur:
            cur.execute("""
                SELECT
                    schemaname,
                    relname as tablename,
                    seq_scan,
                    seq_tup_read,
                    idx_scan,
                    idx_tup_fetch,
                    pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size(relid)) as total_size
                FROM pg_stat_user_tables
                WHERE seq_scan > idx_scan  -- More seq scans than index scans
                AND seq_tup_read > 10000    -- Scanning significant rows
                ORDER BY seq_tup_read DESC;
            """)
            return cur.fetchall()

    def get_duplicate_indexes(self) -> List[Dict]:
        """Find potentially redundant indexes"""
        with self.conn.cursor(cursor_factory=RealDictCursor) as cur:
            cur.execute("""
                SELECT
                    a.indexname as index_1,
                    b.indexname as index_2,
                    a.tablename
                FROM pg_indexes a
                JOIN pg_indexes b ON a.tablename = b.tablename
                WHERE a.indexname != b.indexname
                AND (
                    -- Same columns
                    a.indexdef = b.indexdef
                    -- Or one is prefix of another
                    OR a.indexdef LIKE b.indexdef || '%'
                    OR b.indexdef LIKE a.indexdef || '%'
                )
                AND a.schemaname = 'public';
            """)
            return cur.fetchall()

    def benchmark_query(self, query: str, iterations: int = 100) -> Dict:
        """Benchmark query performance"""
        times = []

        with self.conn.cursor() as cur:
            for _ in range(iterations):
                start = time.perf_counter()
                cur.execute(query)
                cur.fetchall()
                times.append(time.perf_counter() - start)

        return {
            "min_ms": min(times) * 1000,
            "max_ms": max(times) * 1000,
            "avg_ms": sum(times) / len(times) * 1000,
            "iterations": iterations
        }

# Usage
db = PostgreSQLIndexing("postgresql://user:pass@localhost/mydb")

# Create indexes
db.create_basic_indexes()
db.create_expression_indexes()

# Analyze performance
plan = db.analyze_query("SELECT * FROM customers WHERE email = 'test@example.com'")
print("Query Plan:", plan)

# Find optimization opportunities
unused = db.get_index_usage_stats()
missing = db.find_missing_indexes()
```

sections.title: Example 2: MongoDB Indexing Strategies
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- MongoDB Indexing Best Practices
- Complete guide to MongoDB indexing
- Different types of MongoDB indexes
- ESR Rule: Equality, Sort, Range Order of fields in compound index matters!
- 1. Single field index
- 2. Compound index (ESR rule: Equality, Sort, Range)
- 3. Text index for full-text search
- 5. TTL index (auto-delete old documents)

```python
"""
MongoDB Indexing Best Practices
"""

from pymongo import MongoClient, ASCENDING, DESCENDING, TEXT
from pymongo.collection import Collection
from typing import List, Dict
import time

class MongoDBIndexing:
    """
    Complete guide to MongoDB indexing
    """

    def __init__(self, connection_string: str):
        self.client = MongoClient(connection_string)
        self.db = self.client['indexing_demo']
        self.products = self.db['products']
        self.orders = self.db['orders']

    # ==================== BASIC INDEXES ====================

    def create_basic_indexes(self):
        """Different types of MongoDB indexes"""

        # 1. Single field index
        self.products.create_index("sku", unique=True)

        # 2. Compound index (ESR rule: Equality, Sort, Range)
        self.orders.create_index([
            ("customer_id", ASCENDING),   # Equality first
            ("order_date", DESCENDING),   # Sort second
            ("total", ASCENDING)          # Range last
        ])

        # 3. Text index for full-text search
        self.products.create_index([
            ("name", TEXT),
            ("description", TEXT)
        ])

        # 4. Partial index
        self.orders.create_index(
            "customer_id",
            partialFilterExpression={"status": "pending"}
        )

        # 5. TTL index (auto-delete old documents)
        self.db['sessions'].create_index(
            "created_at",
            expireAfterSeconds=3600  # 1 hour TTL
        )

    # ==================== COMPOUND INDEX OPTIMIZATION ====================

    def demonstrate_esr_rule(self):
        """
        ESR Rule: Equality, Sort, Range
        Order of fields in compound index matters!
        """

        # Query: Find orders for a customer in date range, sorted by date
        # WHERE customer_id = X AND order_date BETWEEN Y AND Z ORDER BY order_date

        # GOOD: ESR order
        self.orders.create_index([
            ("customer_id", ASCENDING),   # Equality (=)
            ("order_date", DESCENDING)    # Sort & Range (BETWEEN)
        ], name="idx_esr_good")

        # BAD: Range before equality
        # self.orders.create_index([
        #     ("order_date", DESCENDING),   # Range first = inefficient
        #     ("customer_id", ASCENDING)
        # ])

        # Explain to verify
        query = {
            "customer_id": "cust_123",
            "order_date": {"$gte": "2024-01-01", "$lte": "2024-01-31"}
        }

        explain = self.orders.find(query).sort("order_date", -1).explain()
        return explain["queryPlanner"]["winningPlan"]

    # ==================== COVERED QUERIES ====================

    def create_covering_index(self):
        """
        Covering index: query uses ONLY index, no document fetch
        """
        # Index covers: customer_id, order_date, total
        self.orders.create_index([
            ("customer_id", ASCENDING),
            ("order_date", DESCENDING),
            ("total", ASCENDING)
        ], name="idx_covering")

        # This query is covered (only uses indexed fields)
        covered_query = self.orders.find(
            {"customer_id": "cust_123"},
            {"_id": 0, "order_date": 1, "total": 1}  # Projection
        ).sort("order_date", -1)

        # Verify with explain
        explain = covered_query.explain()
        # "totalDocsExamined": 0 means covered query
        return explain

    # ==================== MULTIKEY INDEXES (ARRAYS) ====================

    def create_multikey_indexes(self):
        """
        Multikey indexes for array fields
        """
        # Index on array field
        self.products.create_index("tags")

        # Now can query:
        # products.find({"tags": "electronics"})   # Contains
        # products.find({"tags": {"$all": ["new", "sale"]}})  # All of

        # Index on embedded array of objects
        self.orders.create_index("items.product_id")

        # Now can query:
        # orders.find({"items.product_id": "prod_123"})

        # Compound with array (only ONE array field allowed per index)
        self.products.create_index([
            ("category", ASCENDING),   # Scalar
            ("tags", ASCENDING)        # Array - creates multikey index
        ])

    # ==================== GEOSPATIAL INDEXES ====================

    def create_geo_indexes(self):
        """
        Indexes for location-based queries
        """
        # 2dsphere for Earth-like sphere
        self.db['locations'].create_index([("location", "2dsphere")])

        # Insert with GeoJSON
        self.db['locations'].insert_one({
            "name": "Store 1",
            "location": {
                "type": "Point",
                "coordinates": [-73.97, 40.77]  # [longitude, latitude]
            }
        })

        # Query: Find within radius
        nearby = self.db['locations'].find({
            "location": {
                "$near": {
                    "$geometry": {
                        "type": "Point",
                        "coordinates": [-73.96, 40.78]
                    },
                    "$maxDistance": 1000  # meters
                }
            }
        })

        return list(nearby)

    # ==================== INDEX ANALYSIS ====================

    def analyze_indexes(self, collection_name: str) -> List[Dict]:
        """Get index statistics"""
        collection = self.db[collection_name]

        # Get index stats
        stats = collection.aggregate([
            {"$indexStats": {}}
        ])

        return list(stats)

    def find_slow_queries(self) -> List[Dict]:
        """Find queries that need indexes"""
        # Enable profiler first: db.setProfilingLevel(1, 100)
        return list(self.db.system.profile.find({
            "op": "query",
            "millis": {"$gt": 100}  # Slow queries (>100ms)
        }).sort("millis", -1).limit(10))

    def get_index_size(self, collection_name: str) -> Dict:
        """Get index sizes"""
        stats = self.db.command("collStats", collection_name)
        return {
            "total_index_size": stats.get("totalIndexSize"),
            "index_sizes": stats.get("indexSizes", {})
        }

    def suggest_indexes(self, collection_name: str, query: Dict, sort: Dict = None) -> str:
        """
        Generate index suggestion based on query
        Following ESR rule
        """
        equality_fields = []
        range_fields = []
        sort_fields = []

        # Analyze query
        for field, value in query.items():
            if isinstance(value, dict):
                # Range operator
                range_fields.append(field)
            else:
                # Equality
                equality_fields.append(field)

        # Analyze sort
        if sort:
            sort_fields = list(sort.keys())

        # Build suggestion (ESR order)
        index_fields = equality_fields + sort_fields
        for f in range_fields:
            if f not in index_fields:
                index_fields.append(f)

        return f"Suggested index: {index_fields}"

# Usage
db = MongoDBIndexing("mongodb://localhost:27017")

# Create indexes
db.create_basic_indexes()
db.demonstrate_esr_rule()

# Analyze
stats = db.analyze_indexes("orders")
sizes = db.get_index_size("orders")
```

sections.title: Example 3: Index Design Patterns
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- Common Index Design Patterns
- Automated index recommendation system
- Analyze query workload and suggest indexes
- Determine optimal index for a single query Following indexing best practices
- Sort by benefit score
- 1. Equality columns first
- 2. Sort columns next (if not already included)
- 3. Range columns last

**Defines:** `QueryPattern`, `QueryInfo`, `IndexDesigner`

```python
"""
Common Index Design Patterns
"""

from typing import List, Dict
from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import Enum

class QueryPattern(Enum):
    POINT_LOOKUP = "point_lookup"       # WHERE id = X
    RANGE_SCAN = "range_scan"           # WHERE date BETWEEN X AND Y
    PREFIX_SEARCH = "prefix_search"     # WHERE name LIKE 'abc%'
    FULL_TEXT = "full_text"             # Text search
    AGGREGATION = "aggregation"         # GROUP BY, COUNT
    SORTING = "sorting"                 # ORDER BY

@dataclass
class QueryInfo:
    tables: List[str]
    filters: Dict[str, str]  # column: operator
    sort_columns: List[str]
    select_columns: List[str]
    frequency: int  # queries per day

class IndexDesigner:
    """
    Automated index recommendation system
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.existing_indexes: Dict[str, List] = {}
        self.query_log: List[QueryInfo] = []

    def analyze_workload(self, queries: List[QueryInfo]) -> List[Dict]:
        """
        Analyze query workload and suggest indexes
        """
        suggestions = []

        for query in queries:
            suggestion = self._analyze_query(query)
            if suggestion:
                suggestions.append({
                    "query": query,
                    "suggested_index": suggestion,
                    "benefit_score": self._calculate_benefit(query, suggestion)
                })

        # Consolidate overlapping indexes
        consolidated = self._consolidate_indexes(suggestions)

        # Sort by benefit score
        return sorted(consolidated, key=lambda x: x["benefit_score"], reverse=True)

    def _analyze_query(self, query: QueryInfo) -> Dict:
        """
        Determine optimal index for a single query
        Following indexing best practices
        """
        index_columns = []

        # 1. Equality columns first
        equality_cols = [
            col for col, op in query.filters.items()
            if op in ['=', 'IN']
        ]
        index_columns.extend(sorted(equality_cols))  # Sort for consistency

        # 2. Sort columns next (if not already included)
        for col in query.sort_columns:
            if col not in index_columns:
                index_columns.append(col)

        # 3. Range columns last
        range_cols = [
            col for col, op in query.filters.items()
            if op in ['<', '>', '<=', '>=', 'BETWEEN', 'LIKE']
        ]
        for col in range_cols:
            if col not in index_columns:
                index_columns.append(col)

        # 4. Check if covering index is beneficial
        include_cols = []
        if len(query.select_columns) <= 5:  # Small projection
            include_cols = [
                col for col in query.select_columns
                if col not in index_columns
            ]

        return {
            "columns": index_columns,
            "include": include_cols,
            "type": self._determine_index_type(query)
        }

    def _determine_index_type(self, query: QueryInfo) -> str:
        """Determine the best index type"""
        has_text_search = any(
            op == 'MATCH'
            for op in query.filters.values()
        )
        if has_text_search:
            return "GIN"  # Full-text index

        has_json = any(
            '->' in col
            for col in query.filters.keys()
        )
        if has_json:
            return "GIN"  # JSON index

        return "BTREE"  # Default

    def _calculate_benefit(self, query: QueryInfo, index: Dict) -> float:
        """
        Score the benefit of an index
        Higher = more beneficial
        """
        score = 0.0

        # Factor 1: Query frequency
        score += query.frequency * 0.1

        # Factor 2: Number of filtered columns covered
        covered_filters = len([
            col for col in query.filters
            if col in index["columns"]
        ])
        score += covered_filters * 10

        # Factor 3: Covering index bonus
        if index["include"]:
            score += 5

        # Factor 4: Sort column coverage
        if query.sort_columns and query.sort_columns[0] in index["columns"]:
            score += 15

        # Penalty: Wide index (many columns)
        score -= len(index["columns"]) * 2

        return score

    def _consolidate_indexes(self, suggestions: List[Dict]) -> List[Dict]:
        """
        Merge overlapping index suggestions
        """
        # Group by table
        by_table: Dict[str, List] = {}
        for s in suggestions:
            for table in s["query"].tables:
                if table not in by_table:
                    by_table[table] = []
                by_table[table].append(s)

        # For each table, merge indexes with common prefixes
        consolidated = []
        for table, table_suggestions in by_table.items():
            merged = self._merge_prefix_indexes(table_suggestions)
            consolidated.extend(merged)

        return consolidated

    def _merge_prefix_indexes(self, suggestions: List[Dict]) -> List[Dict]:
        """Merge indexes where one is prefix of another"""
        # Sort by columns length descending
        sorted_suggestions = sorted(
            suggestions,
            key=lambda x: len(x["suggested_index"]["columns"]),
            reverse=True
        )

        result = []
        used = set()

        for i, s1 in enumerate(sorted_suggestions):
            if i in used:
                continue

            cols1 = tuple(s1["suggested_index"]["columns"])

            # Check if this index covers others
            for j, s2 in enumerate(sorted_suggestions[i+1:], i+1):
                if j in used:
                    continue
                cols2 = tuple(s2["suggested_index"]["columns"])

                # If cols2 is prefix of cols1, merge
                if cols1[:len(cols2)] == cols2:
                    s1["benefit_score"] += s2["benefit_score"] * 0.5
                    used.add(j)

            result.append(s1)

        return result

    def generate_sql(self, suggestion: Dict, table: str) -> str:
        """Generate CREATE INDEX SQL"""
        columns = ", ".join(suggestion["suggested_index"]["columns"])
        include = ""

        if suggestion["suggested_index"]["include"]:
            include_cols = ", ".join(suggestion["suggested_index"]["include"])
            include = f" INCLUDE ({include_cols})"

        index_type = suggestion["suggested_index"]["type"]

        return f"""
CREATE INDEX idx_{table}_{"_".join(suggestion["suggested_index"]["columns"][:2])}
ON {table} USING {index_type} ({columns}){include};
"""

# Usage
designer = IndexDesigner()

# Define query workload
queries = [
    QueryInfo(
        tables=["orders"],
        filters={"customer_id": "=", "order_date": "BETWEEN"},
        sort_columns=["order_date"],
        select_columns=["id", "total", "status"],
        frequency=10000
    ),
    QueryInfo(
        tables=["orders"],
        filters={"status": "="},
        sort_columns=["created_at"],
        select_columns=["id", "customer_id"],
        frequency=5000
    ),
]

# Get recommendations
suggestions = designer.analyze_workload(queries)
for s in suggestions:
    print(designer.generate_sql(s, "orders"))
```

sections.title: Example 4: Index Monitoring and Maintenance
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- Index Health Monitoring System
- Monitor index health and performance
- Comprehensive index health check
- WITH index_stats AS ( SELECT indexrelid, schemaname, relname as tablename, indexrelname as indexname, idx_scan as usage_count, idx_tup_read as…
- Get table row count
- Get average column sizes
- Estimate: row_count * (col_sizes + pointer overhead)
- Use CONCURRENTLY to avoid locks

**Defines:** `IndexHealth`, `IndexMonitor`

```python
"""
Index Health Monitoring System
"""

import psycopg2
from psycopg2.extras import RealDictCursor
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import List, Dict, Optional
from dataclasses import dataclass
import json

@dataclass
class IndexHealth:
    name: str
    table: str
    size_bytes: int
    usage_count: int
    rows_read: int
    bloat_ratio: float
    last_used: Optional[datetime]
    recommendation: str

class IndexMonitor:
    """
    Monitor index health and performance
    """

    def __init__(self, connection_string: str):
        self.conn = psycopg2.connect(connection_string)

    def get_all_indexes_health(self) -> List[IndexHealth]:
        """Comprehensive index health check"""
        with self.conn.cursor(cursor_factory=RealDictCursor) as cur:
            cur.execute("""
                WITH index_stats AS (
                    SELECT
                        indexrelid,
                        schemaname,
                        relname as tablename,
                        indexrelname as indexname,
                        idx_scan as usage_count,
                        idx_tup_read as rows_read,
                        idx_tup_fetch as rows_fetched,
                        pg_relation_size(indexrelid) as index_size
                    FROM pg_stat_user_indexes
                ),
                index_bloat AS (
                    SELECT
                        indexrelid,
                        CASE
                            WHEN avg_leaf_density < 50 THEN
                                (100 - avg_leaf_density) / 100.0
                            ELSE 0
                        END as bloat_ratio
                    FROM pg_stat_all_indexes
                    LEFT JOIN pg_stat_user_indexes USING (indexrelid)
                )
                SELECT
                    s.*,
                    COALESCE(b.bloat_ratio, 0) as bloat_ratio
                FROM index_stats s
                LEFT JOIN index_bloat b USING (indexrelid)
                ORDER BY usage_count;
            """)

            results = []
            for row in cur.fetchall():
                recommendation = self._get_recommendation(row)
                results.append(IndexHealth(
                    name=row['indexname'],
                    table=row['tablename'],
                    size_bytes=row['index_size'],
                    usage_count=row['usage_count'],
                    rows_read=row['rows_read'],
                    bloat_ratio=row.get('bloat_ratio', 0),
                    last_used=None,  # Would need pg_stat_statements
                    recommendation=recommendation
                ))

            return results

    def _get_recommendation(self, stats: Dict) -> str:
        """Generate recommendation based on stats"""
        if stats['usage_count'] == 0 and stats['index_size'] > 1024 * 1024:
            return "CONSIDER_DROPPING: Unused index consuming space"

        if stats.get('bloat_ratio', 0) > 0.3:
            return "REINDEX: High bloat detected"

        if stats['rows_read'] > 0 and stats['rows_fetched'] / stats['rows_read'] < 0.1:
            return "REVIEW: Low selectivity, may not be effective"

        return "HEALTHY"

    def find_unused_indexes(self, days: int = 30) -> List[Dict]:
        """Find indexes not used in specified period"""
        with self.conn.cursor(cursor_factory=RealDictCursor) as cur:
            cur.execute("""
                SELECT
                    schemaname,
                    relname as tablename,
                    indexrelname as indexname,
                    pg_size_pretty(pg_relation_size(indexrelid)) as size,
                    idx_scan as usage_count
                FROM pg_stat_user_indexes
                WHERE idx_scan = 0
                AND indexrelname NOT LIKE '%_pkey'  -- Keep primary keys
                AND pg_relation_size(indexrelid) > 1024 * 100  -- > 100KB
                ORDER BY pg_relation_size(indexrelid) DESC;
            """)
            return cur.fetchall()

    def find_duplicate_indexes(self) -> List[Dict]:
        """Find indexes that are subsets of other indexes"""
        with self.conn.cursor(cursor_factory=RealDictCursor) as cur:
            cur.execute("""
                WITH index_cols AS (
                    SELECT
                        i.indexrelid,
                        i.indrelid,
                        i.indexrelid::regclass as indexname,
                        i.indrelid::regclass as tablename,
                        array_agg(a.attname ORDER BY k.n) as columns
                    FROM pg_index i
                    CROSS JOIN LATERAL unnest(i.indkey) WITH ORDINALITY AS k(attnum, n)
                    JOIN pg_attribute a ON a.attrelid = i.indrelid AND a.attnum = k.attnum
                    WHERE i.indrelid IN (
                        SELECT oid FROM pg_class WHERE relnamespace = 'public'::regnamespace
                    )
                    GROUP BY i.indexrelid, i.indrelid
                )
                SELECT
                    a.indexname as redundant_index,
                    b.indexname as covering_index,
                    a.tablename,
                    a.columns as redundant_columns,
                    b.columns as covering_columns
                FROM index_cols a
                JOIN index_cols b ON a.indrelid = b.indrelid
                    AND a.indexrelid != b.indexrelid
                WHERE a.columns <@ b.columns  -- a is subset of b
                AND array_length(a.columns, 1) < array_length(b.columns, 1);
            """)
            return cur.fetchall()

    def estimate_index_size(self, table: str, columns: List[str]) -> int:
        """Estimate size of a potential new index"""
        with self.conn.cursor() as cur:
            # Get table row count
            cur.execute(f"SELECT reltuples FROM pg_class WHERE relname = %s", (table,))
            row_count = cur.fetchone()[0]

            # Get average column sizes
            total_col_size = 0
            for col in columns:
                cur.execute("""
                    SELECT avg(pg_column_size(%s))
                    FROM %s
                    LIMIT 1000
                """, (col, table))
                avg_size = cur.fetchone()[0] or 8
                total_col_size += avg_size

            # Estimate: row_count * (col_sizes + pointer overhead)
            # B-tree overhead: ~2x
            estimated_size = int(row_count * (total_col_size + 8) * 2)
            return estimated_size

    def reindex_bloated(self, threshold: float = 0.3):
        """Reindex indexes with high bloat"""
        bloated = self.get_all_indexes_health()

        for idx in bloated:
            if idx.bloat_ratio > threshold:
                print(f"Reindexing {idx.name} (bloat: {idx.bloat_ratio:.1%})")

                # Use CONCURRENTLY to avoid locks
                self.conn.autocommit = True
                try:
                    with self.conn.cursor() as cur:
                        cur.execute(f"REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY {idx.name};")
                except Exception as e:
                    print(f"Error reindexing {idx.name}: {e}")
                finally:
                    self.conn.autocommit = False

    def generate_health_report(self) -> Dict:
        """Generate comprehensive health report"""
        health = self.get_all_indexes_health()
        unused = self.find_unused_indexes()
        duplicates = self.find_duplicate_indexes()

        total_index_size = sum(h.size_bytes for h in health)
        unused_size = sum(
            next(
                (h.size_bytes for h in health if h.name == u['indexname']),
                0
            )
            for u in unused
        )

        return {
            "generated_at": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "summary": {
                "total_indexes": len(health),
                "healthy_indexes": len([h for h in health if h.recommendation == "HEALTHY"]),
                "unused_indexes": len(unused),
                "duplicate_indexes": len(duplicates),
                "total_index_size_mb": total_index_size / (1024 * 1024),
                "potential_savings_mb": unused_size / (1024 * 1024)
            },
            "unused_indexes": unused,
            "duplicate_indexes": duplicates,
            "bloated_indexes": [
                {"name": h.name, "bloat": h.bloat_ratio}
                for h in health if h.bloat_ratio > 0.2
            ],
            "recommendations": [
                {"name": h.name, "action": h.recommendation}
                for h in health if h.recommendation != "HEALTHY"
            ]
        }

# Usage
monitor = IndexMonitor("postgresql://user:pass@localhost/mydb")

# Get health report
report = monitor.generate_health_report()
print(json.dumps(report, indent=2, default=str))

# Find issues
unused = monitor.find_unused_indexes()
print(f"Found {len(unused)} unused indexes")

duplicates = monitor.find_duplicate_indexes()
print(f"Found {len(duplicates)} duplicate indexes")
```

sections.title: Example 5: Query Optimization with Indexes
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- Query Optimization Through Indexing
- Analyze and optimize queries through indexing
- Deep analysis of query execution
- Generate optimization suggestions
- Check for sequential scans
- Extract columns from filter
- Check for sort operations without index
- Check for hash joins (might benefit from index)

**Defines:** `QueryAnalysis`, `QueryOptimizer`

```python
"""
Query Optimization Through Indexing
"""

import psycopg2
from psycopg2.extras import RealDictCursor
import re
from typing import List, Dict, Tuple
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass
class QueryAnalysis:
    query: str
    execution_time_ms: float
    scan_type: str
    rows_estimated: int
    rows_actual: int
    index_used: str
    suggestions: List[str]

class QueryOptimizer:
    """
    Analyze and optimize queries through indexing
    """

    def __init__(self, connection_string: str):
        self.conn = psycopg2.connect(connection_string)

    def analyze_query(self, query: str) -> QueryAnalysis:
        """
        Deep analysis of query execution
        """
        with self.conn.cursor(cursor_factory=RealDictCursor) as cur:
            # Get execution plan
            cur.execute(f"EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, FORMAT JSON) {query}")
            plan_json = cur.fetchone()['QUERY PLAN'][0]

            plan = plan_json['Plan']

            return QueryAnalysis(
                query=query,
                execution_time_ms=plan_json.get('Execution Time', 0),
                scan_type=plan.get('Node Type', 'Unknown'),
                rows_estimated=plan.get('Plan Rows', 0),
                rows_actual=plan.get('Actual Rows', 0),
                index_used=plan.get('Index Name', 'None'),
                suggestions=self._generate_suggestions(plan, query)
            )

    def _generate_suggestions(self, plan: Dict, query: str) -> List[str]:
        """Generate optimization suggestions"""
        suggestions = []

        # Check for sequential scans
        if plan.get('Node Type') == 'Seq Scan':
            table = plan.get('Relation Name')
            filter_cond = plan.get('Filter', '')

            # Extract columns from filter
            columns = self._extract_filter_columns(filter_cond)
            if columns:
                suggestions.append(
                    f"Consider adding index on {table}({', '.join(columns)})"
                )

        # Check for sort operations without index
        if plan.get('Node Type') == 'Sort':
            sort_key = plan.get('Sort Key', [])
            suggestions.append(
                f"Sort operation detected. Consider index including {sort_key}"
            )

        # Check for hash joins (might benefit from index)
        if 'Hash' in plan.get('Node Type', ''):
            suggestions.append(
                "Hash join detected. Index on join columns might improve performance"
            )

        # Check estimation accuracy
        estimated = plan.get('Plan Rows', 1)
        actual = plan.get('Actual Rows', 1)
        if actual > 0 and abs(estimated - actual) / actual > 0.5:
            suggestions.append(
                f"Row estimation off by {abs(estimated-actual)/actual:.0%}. "
                "Consider running ANALYZE on the table"
            )

        # Recursively check child plans
        for child in plan.get('Plans', []):
            suggestions.extend(self._generate_suggestions(child, query))

        return suggestions

    def _extract_filter_columns(self, filter_expr: str) -> List[str]:
        """Extract column names from filter expression"""
        # Simple regex to find column references
        # Format: (column_name = value) or (column_name > value)
        pattern = r'\((\w+)\s*[=<>!]+'
        matches = re.findall(pattern, filter_expr)
        return list(set(matches))

    def compare_with_without_index(
        self,
        query: str,
        index_name: str
    ) -> Dict:
        """
        Compare query performance with and without an index
        """
        with self.conn.cursor() as cur:
            # Disable index
            cur.execute(f"UPDATE pg_index SET indisvalid = false WHERE indexrelid = '{index_name}'::regclass")
            self.conn.commit()

            # Run without index
            without_result = self.analyze_query(query)

            # Re-enable index
            cur.execute(f"UPDATE pg_index SET indisvalid = true WHERE indexrelid = '{index_name}'::regclass")
            self.conn.commit()

            # Run with index
            with_result = self.analyze_query(query)

            return {
                "without_index": {
                    "time_ms": without_result.execution_time_ms,
                    "scan_type": without_result.scan_type
                },
                "with_index": {
                    "time_ms": with_result.execution_time_ms,
                    "scan_type": with_result.scan_type,
                    "index_used": with_result.index_used
                },
                "improvement": f"{(without_result.execution_time_ms / max(with_result.execution_time_ms, 0.001)):.1f}x faster"
            }

    def suggest_index_for_query(self, query: str) -> str:
        """
        Generate CREATE INDEX statement for a query
        """
        # Parse query to extract components
        tables = self._extract_tables(query)
        where_cols = self._extract_where_columns(query)
        order_cols = self._extract_order_columns(query)
        select_cols = self._extract_select_columns(query)

        if not tables or not where_cols:
            return "-- Cannot suggest index: unable to parse query"

        table = tables[0]

        # Follow ESR rule
        index_cols = []

        # Equality columns first
        equality_cols = [c for c, op in where_cols if op == '=']
        index_cols.extend(equality_cols)

        # Sort columns next
        for col in order_cols:
            if col not in index_cols:
                index_cols.append(col)

        # Range columns last
        range_cols = [c for c, op in where_cols if op in ['<', '>', '<=', '>=', 'BETWEEN']]
        for col in range_cols:
            if col not in index_cols:
                index_cols.append(col)

        # Include columns for covering
        include_cols = [c for c in select_cols if c not in index_cols and c != '*']

        col_str = ", ".join(index_cols)
        include_str = f" INCLUDE ({', '.join(include_cols)})" if include_cols else ""

        return f"CREATE INDEX idx_{table}_suggestion ON {table}({col_str}){include_str};"

    def _extract_tables(self, query: str) -> List[str]:
        """Extract table names from FROM clause"""
        pattern = r'FROM\s+(\w+)'
        match = re.search(pattern, query, re.IGNORECASE)
        if match:
            return [match.group(1)]
        return []

    def _extract_where_columns(self, query: str) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
        """Extract column and operator from WHERE clause"""
        # Simple pattern: column = value, column > value, etc.
        pattern = r'(\w+)\s*([=<>!]+|BETWEEN|LIKE|IN)'
        where_match = re.search(r'WHERE\s+(.+?)(?:ORDER|GROUP|LIMIT|$)', query, re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)
        if not where_match:
            return []

        where_clause = where_match.group(1)
        matches = re.findall(pattern, where_clause, re.IGNORECASE)
        return [(m[0], m[1]) for m in matches]

    def _extract_order_columns(self, query: str) -> List[str]:
        """Extract columns from ORDER BY"""
        pattern = r'ORDER\s+BY\s+([\w,\s]+?)(?:ASC|DESC|LIMIT|$)'
        match = re.search(pattern, query, re.IGNORECASE)
        if match:
            cols = match.group(1).split(',')
            return [c.strip().split()[0] for c in cols]
        return []

    def _extract_select_columns(self, query: str) -> List[str]:
        """Extract columns from SELECT"""
        pattern = r'SELECT\s+(.+?)\s+FROM'
        match = re.search(pattern, query, re.IGNORECASE)
        if match:
            cols = match.group(1).split(',')
            return [c.strip().split()[-1] for c in cols]  # Handle aliases
        return []

    def batch_optimize(self, queries: List[str]) -> Dict:
        """
        Analyze multiple queries and suggest consolidated indexes
        """
        all_suggestions = {}

        for query in queries:
            analysis = self.analyze_query(query)
            if analysis.scan_type == 'Seq Scan':
                tables = self._extract_tables(query)
                if tables:
                    table = tables[0]
                    if table not in all_suggestions:
                        all_suggestions[table] = []
                    all_suggestions[table].append(
                        self.suggest_index_for_query(query)
                    )

        # Consolidate suggestions per table
        consolidated = {}
        for table, suggestions in all_suggestions.items():
            # Deduplicate and merge similar indexes
            consolidated[table] = list(set(suggestions))

        return consolidated

# Usage
optimizer = QueryOptimizer("postgresql://user:pass@localhost/mydb")

# Analyze a query
query = """
    SELECT id, name, email
    FROM customers
    WHERE country = 'USA' AND status = 'active'
    ORDER BY created_at DESC
    LIMIT 100
"""

analysis = optimizer.analyze_query(query)
print(f"Execution time: {analysis.execution_time_ms}ms")
print(f"Scan type: {analysis.scan_type}")
print(f"Suggestions: {analysis.suggestions}")

# Get index suggestion
suggestion = optimizer.suggest_index_for_query(query)
print(f"Suggested index: {suggestion}")
```

sections.body:
### Index Type Selection

| Query Pattern       | Recommended Index |
| ------------------- | ----------------- |
| `column = value`    | B-tree            |
| `column IN (...)`   | B-tree            |
| `column < value`    | B-tree            |
| `column BETWEEN`    | B-tree            |
| `column IS NULL`    | B-tree            |
| `LIKE 'prefix%'`    | B-tree            |
| `LIKE '%anywhere%'` | GIN (trigram)     |
| `@@ tsquery`        | GIN (full-text)   |
| `@> jsonb`          | GIN               |
| `ST_Distance`       | GiST (spatial)    |
| Array contains      | GIN               |

quiz.question: How do indexes improve query performance?
options: Strategy for mixed workload: Minimize indexes on write-heavy tables; Only essential indexes; Use partial indexes where possible.
Don't index when: Small tables: Full scan faster than index lookup; Low selectivity: Index reads too many rows.
Ordering guidelines: Most selective columns first (filter most rows); Equality conditions before range conditions; Frequently filtered columns first.

Indexes improve performance by: Reducing I/O: Instead of scanning entire table, read only index pages; Order preservation: B-tree maintains sorted order, enabling efficient range scans; Binary search: O(log n) vs O(n) for full scan.
quiz.explanation: Indexes improve performance by: Reducing I/O: Instead of scanning entire table, read only index pages Order preservation: B-tree maintains sorted order, enabling efficient range scans Binary search: O(log n) vs O(n) for full scan Example: Trade-offs: Slower writes (must update indexes) Extra storage space Maintenance overhead (bloat, fragmentation) ---

quiz.question: What is a covering index and when would you use it?
options: Selectivity = Number of distinct values / Total rows
Don't index when: Small tables: Full scan faster than index lookup; Low selectivity: Index reads too many rows.
partial index** indexes only a subset of rows matching a predicate.
covering index** contains all columns needed by a query, eliminating the need to access the table data.
quiz.explanation: covering index** contains all columns needed by a query, eliminating the need to access the table data. Benefits: Index-only scan (no table access) 2-5x faster for covered queries When to use: Frequently executed queries Queries selecting few columns Read-heavy workloads When NOT to use: Wide selection (many columns) Frequently updated included columns Storage-constrained systems ---

quiz.question: Explain the difference between B-tree and Hash indexes.
options: PostgreSQL JSONB: MongoDB: Query patterns: ---
Too Many Indexes Problems: Slower writes; Each INSERT updates all indexes; Each UPDATE might update multiple indexes.
Ordering guidelines: Most selective columns first (filter most rows); Equality conditions before range conditions; Frequently filtered columns first.
When to use Hash: Only equality comparisons; Very large tables (marginal performance gain); Memory-resident data.
quiz.explanation: When to use Hash: Only equality comparisons Very large tables (marginal performance gain) Memory-resident data When to use B-tree (default): Range queries needed Sorting needed General purpose ---
